headline: Bush addresses Ukraine's Supreme Soviet in Kiev
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 1 August 1991 carried a Moscow INTERFAX preview of Bush's arrival in Ukraine: Foreign Minister Zlenko welcoming the visit as a landmark for direct contacts, and RUKH's Ivan Drach doubting it, since the Bush administration kept stressing that stability lay in Moscow.

headline: Iraq invades Kuwait
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 2 August 1990 carried Cairo MENA reports on the Arab League's emergency session over "the Iraqi forces' entry into Kuwait," Kuwait's request for joint Arab forces, and a Kuwaiti minister saying street fighting continued.

headline: Baker and Shevardnadze issue a joint statement condemning Iraq
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 3 August 1990 carried Moscow TASS in English on Bush condemning the invasion of Kuwait and freezing Iraqi and Kuwaiti assets, noting he was pleased with the Soviet reaction, and a Moscow World Service item that Baker would stop in Moscow for a planned joint statement.

headline: Croatia launches Operation Storm against Krajina
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 4 August 1995 listed a long run of Croatia items on the Krajina offensive: Tudjman announcing "military-police measures," Serb lines broken at 30 sites, Belgrade radio on the shelling of Knin, and Akashi calling the offensive hard to understand.

headline: Croatian forces take Knin
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 7 August 1995 carried AFP on UN mediator Stoltenberg shuttling between Belgrade and Zagreb as Croatia shelled Knin, and Belgrade TANJUG accusing Washington of giving "direct support" to Croatian aggression; the fall of Knin is not on this page.

headline: UN Resolution 661 imposes sanctions on Iraq
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 8 August 1990 carried Moscow TASS in English on Perez de Cuellar circulating Resolution 661's sanctions against Iraq to all member states, recalling the Rhodesia and South Africa precedents, and a Kuwaiti message on Iraqi mistreatment of civilians.

headline: Central American presidents sign the Esquipulas II peace plan
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 7 August 1987 carried Guatemalan radio on the Central American presidents' arrival for the Esquipulas II summit and an ACAN-EFE report of some 1,000 Nicaraguan exiles and anticommunists protesting Ortega's presence.

headline: Saddam's son-in-law Husayn Kamil defects to Jordan
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 10 August 1995 carried Baghdad INA announcing Husayn Kamil Hasan's dismissal, AFP reporting Jordan's grant of asylum and his first statement that Saddam's government had "lost its credibility," and Radio Monte Carlo citing family differences.

headline: Iraq announces the merger of Kuwait
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 8 August 1990 carried Riyadh SPA's account of the Gulf Cooperation Council's 7 August Jeddah session condemning Iraq's occupation of Kuwait and demanding immediate withdrawal; the merger announcement itself is not on the page.
doubt: Page carries GCC condemnation of the occupation; the merger announcement is not reported

headline: UN announces an Iran-Iraq ceasefire date
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 8 August 1988 led with Baghdad radio's message from Saddam Husayn offering a cease-fire if Iran agreed to direct talks, and Tehran radio reporting that the UN secretary general meant to announce a cease-fire date by 9 August.

headline: Hosokawa takes office as Japan's first non-LDP prime minister since 1955
fbis: The East Asia Daily Report of 9 August 1993 carried the KYODO roster of Morihiro Hosokawa's new coalition cabinet, with each minister's party, ahead of the emperor's attestation ceremony that afternoon.

headline: Cairo Arab summit votes to send forces to defend Saudi Arabia
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 10 August 1990 carried items on the eve of the Cairo summit: Rabat MAP on Klibi leaving for the emergency summit on Iraq's "annexation of Kuwait," Riyadh radio asserting the GCC states' freedom to secure themselves, and arrivals of Arab leaders.

headline: American hostage Edward Tracy freed in Lebanon
Martial law declared in Isfahan
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 14 August 1978 carried an AFP report of a curfew in Esfahan after rioters ransacked the Shah Abbas Hotel, and Tehran radio's government statement declaring a month of martial law in the city.

headline: Saddam links withdrawal from Kuwait to Israel's occupied territories
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 13 August 1990 carried Palestinian reaction to Saddam's linkage proposal: PLO factions denouncing US plans, the PLO envoy in Rome calling it the moment to settle all occupations, and Radio Monte Carlo quoting West Bank figures praising "the Iraqi proposal."

headline: Israel's heaviest bombardment of West Beirut
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 12 August 1982 led with Israeli radio on Begin's talks with Habib over the PLO evacuation plan and Sharon on French troops; it does not report the day's bombardment of West Beirut.
doubt: Page covers evacuation negotiations; the bombardment is not reported

headline: Bomb destroys a Palestinian group's building in Beirut
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 14 August 1978 carried, in fragmentary OCR, UPI on a nine-floor building in Beirut's al-Fakihani area destroyed by a blast that killed many, and Voice of Palestine on the PLO forming a committee to investigate it.

headline: Carlos the Jackal seized in Sudan and flown to France
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 15 August 1994 carried Khartoum SUNA on the Sudanese interior minister announcing the arrest of "Carlos," wanted by France for killing two Frenchmen, and Cairo MENA confirming the man handed to France was Ilich Ramirez, who had entered on a forged passport.

headline: Strike begins at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdansk
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 15 August 1980 carried Warsaw radio acknowledging "work stoppages" including sections of the Gdansk shipyard, and a Paris AFP report that 17,000 Gdansk shipyard workers had struck over the dismissal of Anna Walentynowicz.

headline: Saddam offers Iran the 1975 border and a prisoner exchange
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 15 August 1990 carried Baghdad radio's text of Saddam Husayn's letter to Rafsanjani offering a comprehensive settlement with Iran, framed as removing obstacles so Iraq's forces could face "the great battle."

headline: Iraq orders Westerners in Kuwait to gather at hotels
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 17 August 1990 carried items on occupied Kuwait: an INA curfew order for Kuwait City, claims of resistance captures, and an Israel Radio interview with a Kuwaiti royal describing Iraqi looting; the order gathering Westerners at hotels is not on the page.
doubt: Page covers occupied Kuwait generally; the hotel order for Westerners is not reported

headline: King Husayn meets Bush at Kennebunkport
Pakistan's President Zia killed in plane crash
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 17 August 1988 carried Pakistani radio's report that Zia had died in a crash with senior generals and US Ambassador Raphel, Ghulam Ishaq Khan assuming the presidency, and an earlier BBC report of the rumored crash.

headline: Colombian presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galan assassinated
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 21 August 1989 carried, under Colombia, a Madrid EFE report that Liberal presidential hopeful Luis Carlos Galan had been shot as he was about to speak in the main square of Soacha, south of Bogota.

headline: Plotters isolate Gorbachev at Foros
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 20 August 1991 carried a Soviet television report of 19 August showing Yeltsin reading his decree branding the emergency committee's actions a coup, demanding that Gorbachev, "locked in his dacha in Foros," be allowed to speak, and Muscovites building barricades.

headline: State Emergency Committee seizes power in Moscow
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 19 August 1991 carried Moscow TASS in English with Yanayev's statement assuming presidential duties because of Gorbachev's "inability for health reasons," followed by an AFP profile of Yanayev.

headline: US Navy jets shoot down two Libyan fighters over the Gulf of Sidra
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 19 August 1981 carried Tripoli radio's version: two Libyan aircraft on a routine reconnaissance flight intercepted and fired on by eight US aircraft over Libyan territory and waters during Sixth Fleet maneuvers in the Gulf of Sidra.

headline: Estonia declares independence during the coup
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 20 August 1991 carried a TASS roundup of regional reaction to the emergency, including Tallinn radio on Estonia's Emergency Defense Council pledging peaceful restoration of independence; the independence declaration itself is not on this page.
doubt: Page shows an Estonian council statement; the declaration of independence is not reported here

headline: Iran-Iraq ceasefire takes effect
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 22 August 1988 listed under Iran reportage on the cease-fire's implementation: UN observers arriving, UN troops deployed, "Cease-Fire in Effect," and Khamene'i on its observance.

headline: The August coup collapses
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 21 August 1991 carried the emergency committee still issuing orders on 20 August: cancelling a Russian MVD order to move armed formations into Moscow, and Decision No. 4 restricting broadcasting; the collapse is not yet reported.
doubt: Page shows the committee still in control on 20 August, not its collapse

headline: Latvia declares independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 21 August 1991 carried Tallinn radio and INTERFAX on Estonia's Supreme Council proclaiming state independence by 69 votes, and Baltic leaders preparing governments in exile with Latvia's Dainis Ivans named; Latvia's own declaration is not on the page.
doubt: Page reports Estonia's declaration, not Latvia's

headline: Crowds topple Dzerzhinskiy's statue outside KGB headquarters
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 23 August 1991 carried Russian Television on crowds flooding Dzerzhinskiy Square and besieging the CPSU Central Committee, and Moscow INTERFAX reporting that the Dzerzhinskiy statue had been dismantled at 23:30 on the city's decision.

headline: KGB chief Kryuchkov arrested with the coup plotters
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 22 August 1991 carried Radio Mayak relaying Reuters on the arrests of Yanayev, Yazov, Kryuchkov, Tizyakov and Pugo, Radio Moscow announcing Kryuchkov's arrest, and TASS reporting Pugo's suicide as officials came to detain him.

headline: Baltic Way human chain on the pact's 50th anniversary
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 23 August 1989 carried Tallinn radio's People's Front statement inviting Russian-speakers to join that night's human chain of the "Baltic wave," after TASS quoting Yakovlev that the 1939 pact did not determine the Baltic states' status.

headline: Ukraine declares independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 26 August 1991 previewed the post-coup Supreme Soviet session, noting that "the Ukraine's independence proclaimed by the republican parliament" had changed the balance on the Union treaty; the declaration gets only that passing mention.

headline: Gorbachev resigns as CPSU general secretary
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 26 August 1991 carried Moscow TASS on Lukyanov defending his conduct in the coup, deputies nominating Yakovlev and Shevardnadze to top posts, and a constitutional official calling the CPSU leadership "the plot's main figure"; Gorbachev's resignation is not on this page.
doubt: Page covers Lukyanov and nominations; Gorbachev's resignation is not reported here

headline: Sejm confirms Mazowiecki as Poland's prime minister
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 24 August 1989 carried a report that Jaruzelski had written to the Sejm marshal proposing that parliament accept Kiszczak's resignation and elect Tadeusz Mazowiecki prime minister, after PZPR remarks on keeping the interior and defense ministries.

headline: Belorussia declares independence
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 26 August 1991 carried Radio Mayak and INTERFAX on the Belorussian Supreme Soviet's extraordinary session and a 50,000-strong Minsk rally, then a Vremya report that the parliament had suspended the republic's Communist Party and adopted a decision on independence.

headline: UN Resolution 665 authorizes enforcing the Iraq embargo at sea
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 27 August 1990 carried Egyptian Foreign Minister Abd-al-Majid reviewing the Gulf crisis, citing the Security Council's resolutions "from Resolution 660 all the way to Resolution 665" and Egypt's commitment to Kuwait's liberation.

headline: Cardinal Luciani elected Pope John Paul I
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 29 August 1978 carried East Berlin ADN on Erich Honecker's telegram of good wishes to Pope John Paul I on his election, expressing hope for his contribution to peace and detente.

headline: USSR Supreme Soviet opens its post-coup session
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 26 August 1991 previewed the USSR Supreme Soviet's post-coup session as "very heated," with the party's fate and the Union treaty on the agenda, and carried INTERFAX on new information implicating parliament chairman Lukyanov in the coup.

headline: IRA bomb kills Lord Mountbatten
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 28 August 1979 listed under Czechoslovakia an item that the Mountbatten assassination would lead to "stepped-up repression".

headline: Iraq declares Kuwait its 19th province
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 30 August 1990 carried an Egyptian commentary answering the Iraqi media and denouncing the "robbing" of Kuwait by armed force, its annexation and conversion into "Iraq's 19th province."

headline: Menachem Begin announces his resignation
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 29 August 1983 led with Jerusalem radio on Begin's announcement at the 28 August Cabinet meeting that he would resign, ministers' efforts to dissuade him, and Shamir named as the likely successor.

headline: USSR Supreme Soviet suspends the Communist Party's activities
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 29 August 1991 carried Moscow TASS in English on the Supreme Soviet's special session: the Russian Communist leader denying any coup role, Lukyanov insisting he was no plotter, and tension with Ukraine over Russian border claims; the suspension vote itself is not on this page.
doubt: Page covers the special session's debate; the suspension vote is not reported

headline: KGB arrests US correspondent Nicholas Daniloff in Moscow
fbis: The Soviet Union contents for September 1986 listed under United States & Canada an item that IZVESTIYA had reported Daniloff's arrest for "espionage," amid commentary on US anti-Libya activities.

headline: Bomb kills Iran's President Raja'i and Prime Minister Bahonar
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 31 August 1981 led with Tehran radio reporting that President Raja'i and Prime Minister Bahonar were killed by a bomb in the Prime Ministry, blamed on "hypocrites of the left and right," and AFP on a disputed Mojahedin claim of responsibility.

headline: Arafat leaves Beirut
fbis: The Middle East review in the Daily Report of 30 August 1982 led with Beirut radio announcing Arafat's departure after a farewell meeting with Prime Minister al-Wazzan, and AFP citing WAFA on his warning that the "earth will shake in several places."

headline: Gdansk Agreement signed with the strikers
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 2 September 1980 carried Gdansk radio's recording of the 30 August shipyard meeting between Jagielski's government commission and Walesa's strike committee, with Andrzej Gwiazda reading the agreed terms for new self-governing trade unions.

headline: Last Russian troops leave Germany
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 31 August 1994 carried an ITAR-TASS press review on the farewell ceremony for the last Russian troops leaving Germany, quoting Yeltsin that "an epoch of enmity" was ending, and KRASNAYA ZVEZDA on 338,000 troops withdrawn.
